In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed depression in the total number and percentage of nucleated BM cell is the net result of a complex situation that reflects the differential effects of BZ exposure on the cells of all three hematopoietic cell lineages, with a significant depression in the lymphocytes and the erythroid lineage, and a stimulation of granulopoieses.

BZ causes a depression of BM cell numbers that is a reflection of a complex situation involving a depression in the number of lymphocytes and erythroid precursors, and an increase in the numbers of intermediate granulocytic precursors and terminally differentiated neutrophils.

benzene causes a significant depression of bone marrow cellularity that is due to a suppression of the development of all of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells except those of the granulocyte lineage, and the observed effects of interleukins on the process are complex and dependent on the dose, the time of administration, and the lineage of the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BZ causes depression of the BM cellularity, and this effect is mediated by HQ, which inhibits processing of pre- IL-1α into the active cytokine, IL-1α.

BZ-induced BM depression is due to a lack of the IL-1α signal that is necessary for the production of colony-stimulating activities by the stromal fibrolast, which are necessary for the survival of the pluripotent and multipotential progenitor cells.
BZ-induced BM depression occurs because of a failure of the stromal cells to produce IL-1α, and this failure is due to the inhibition of IL- 1α processing by HQ.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BZ-induced inhibition in the production of IL-1 is the cause of the overall depression of the BM cellularity, which is reflected in the decreased number of lymphocytes and erythroid cells, and the increased numbers of granulocytes.
the observed depression in BM cellularity is not due to an overall suppression of hematopoiesis, but rather a specific suppression of lymphopoiesis and erythropoiesis.

the observed depression of BM cell numbers in BZ-treated mice is the result of an inhibition of IL- 1α production and processing by the stromal cells, and that IL-1α is a key cytokine in the regulation of the development of all the hematopoietically committed cells.
